# Zindel Lab

> The Zindel Lab at ETH Zürich (Department of Biology, D-BIOL; Institute of Molecular Health Sciences) studies tissue repair, fibrosis, and foreign-body responses at the interface of immunity and the body cavities. The lab is led by Prof. Dr. Joel Zindel, a surgeon-scientist, and is known for intravital microscopy of immune and mesothelial cell dynamics in living mice. Website: https://zindellab.ch

## About

- **Name:** Zindel Lab (Zindel Laboratory)
- **Principal investigator:** Prof. Dr. Joel Zindel — trained as a surgeon (MD, University of Bern), founded the lab in Bern in 2023, moved to ETH Zürich in August 2025.
- **Institution:** ETH Zürich, Institute of Molecular Health Sciences, Department of Biology (D-BIOL).
- **Location:** Otto-Stern-Weg 7, HPL F 32.2, 8093 Zürich, Switzerland.
- **Mission:** Improve patient outcomes after surgery by uncovering the cellular and molecular mechanisms of tissue repair, regeneration, and foreign-body biology.

## Research themes

- **Cavity macrophage aggregation:** GATA6+ peritoneal macrophages and the macrophage disappearance reaction; scavenger receptors MARCO and MSR1; calcium dependence; conservation to sea urchin coelomocytes.
- **Mesothelial to mesenchymal transition (MMT):** how mesothelial cells reprogram into scar-forming myofibroblasts after surgery; role of the peritoneal microenvironment and EGFR signaling.
- **Foreign body reaction and implant lifetime:** how implant surface properties shape the local immune response, with bioengineering collaborators.
- **Translational studies:** prospective patient cohorts (with Inselspital Bern) and a human peritoneal cell biobank; the mouse-to-human translational gap.

## Methods

- Intravital (multiphoton) microscopy — Leica Stellaris DIVE, 12 kHz resonant scanner, FLIM.
- Quantitative 4D image analysis — custom cell segmentation, classification, and tracking on ETH HPC.
- Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics (scRNA-seq, pySCENIC regulon inference).
- Murine models: focal peritoneal injury (FPI) and peritoneal button (PB) adhesion models.
- Human peritoneal fluid and tissue sampling via clinical collaborations.
